definition: Wrapping each type of prompt content in its own tag, such as `<instructions>` or `<context>`, so Claude can parse a complex prompt unambiguously.
whyItMatters: Reduces misinterpretation when instructions, context, examples and variable inputs share one prompt. Use consistent, descriptive tag names.
example: Nest for hierarchy: `<documents>` holds each `<document index="1">`, with its source and content in their own tags.

definition: Replaces the older turns of a conversation with a summary Claude writes on the server, so you need no summarization code of your own.
whyItMatters: Keeps a long conversation or agent task inside the context window. **On demand**, you decide when to compact; **at a token threshold**, the API does.
example: On-demand compaction uses the top-level `compaction` parameter and the `compact-2026-09-04` beta header.

definition: A context editing strategy, `clear_tool_uses_20250919`, that clears the oldest tool results once context passes a threshold, leaving placeholder text.
whyItMatters: Fits agents with heavy tool use whose old results are no longer needed. Defaults: trigger at **100,000** input tokens, keep the **3** most recent tool uses.
example: List a tool in `exclude_tools` if its uses and results must never be cleared.

definition: An Anthropic-provided, client-side tool: Claude requests file operations under `/memories`, and your application executes them on storage you control.
whyItMatters: Memory lives entirely in your application, so it persists only if your handler serves the same store. The handler must reject paths outside `/memories`.
example: Tools entry: `{"type": "memory_20250818", "name": "memory"}`, with no input schema of your own.

definition: An agent keeps lightweight identifiers (file paths, stored queries, web links) and uses tools to load the data into context at runtime.
whyItMatters: Keeps context focused and enables progressive disclosure. The trade-off: runtime exploration is slower than retrieving pre-computed data.
example: Claude Code drops CLAUDE.md in up front, then uses glob and grep to retrieve files just in time.

source.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents

definition: The zone between brittle, hardcoded if-else logic and vague guidance that falsely assumes shared context.
whyItMatters: Anthropic's advice: be specific enough to guide behavior yet flexible enough to give strong heuristics. Minimal doesn't necessarily mean short.
example: Start with a minimal prompt on the best model, then add instructions and examples for the failure modes you find.

source.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents

definition: A curated set of self-contained tools with minimal overlap in functionality, so it's clear which tool fits each situation.
whyItMatters: Bloated tool sets are a common failure mode: if a human engineer can't definitively say which tool to use, an agent can't be expected to do better.

source.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents

definition: Explaining the motivation for an instruction, such as why a behavior matters, so Claude better understands your goal.
whyItMatters: Claude is smart enough to generalize from the explanation. The guide's example: say replies go to a text-to-speech engine, not just "NEVER use ellipses".

definition: Setting a role in the system prompt, such as "You are a helpful coding assistant specializing in Python", to focus Claude's behavior and tone.
whyItMatters: The lightest fix when answers are too generic for your use case: even a single sentence makes a difference.
example: The guide's example sends the role as `system` in the Messages API request.

definition: A partial assistant message on the last turn for Claude to continue from. Not supported starting with Claude 4.6 models: those requests return a 400.
whyItMatters: Migrate: structured outputs for formats, tools with an `enum` or structured outputs for classification, system prompt instructions to skip preambles.
example: Earlier models still accept prefills, and assistant messages elsewhere in the conversation are unaffected.

definition: For long-document tasks, asking Claude to quote the relevant parts of the documents first, before it carries out the task.
whyItMatters: Helps Claude focus on the relevant content and ignore the rest. Pair it with long data at the top of the prompt, above the query.
example: Ask for relevant quotes in `<quotes>` tags, then for the analysis based on them in `<info>` tags.

definition: When thinking is off, asking Claude to think through a problem step by step, with tags like `<thinking>` and `<answer>` to separate reasoning from output.
whyItMatters: The guide's fallback when thinking is off. With thinking on, general instructions like "think thoroughly" often beat a hand-written step-by-step plan.

definition: Claude Opus 4.5 and Claude Opus 4.6 are more responsive to the system prompt, so wording written to fix undertriggering can make them overtrigger.
whyItMatters: Dial back aggressive language: replace "CRITICAL: You MUST use this tool when..." with "Use this tool when...". Lower effort only as a fallback.

term: Structured outputs that miss the schema
definition: Structured outputs guarantee compliance in most cases, but a refusal or a `max_tokens` cut-off can return output that doesn't match your schema.
whyItMatters: Check `stop_reason` before parsing. A refusal still returns HTTP 200 and is billed; for `max_tokens`, retry with a higher limit.

definition: Setting `strict: true` on a tool definition constrains sampling so Claude's tool inputs strictly follow the tool's `input_schema`.
whyItMatters: Without it, Claude might send `"2"` instead of `2` or omit required fields. With it, there's no need to validate and retry tool calls.
example: Add `"strict": true` at the top level of the tool, alongside `name`, `description` and `input_schema`.

definition: Structured outputs don't guarantee the capitalization of string `enum` and `const` values: a value may differ from your schema only in case.
whyItMatters: Nothing flags it: the response completes with no error and no special stop_reason. Compare case-insensitively and avoid values that differ only in case.
example: Schema says "Conversation topic 3"; the reply may say "Conversation Topic 3".

definition: Explicitly giving Claude permission to admit uncertainty, for example to say it doesn't have enough information, instead of answering anyway.
whyItMatters: A basic hallucination-reduction technique that can drastically reduce false information. Such techniques reduce hallucinations but don't eliminate them.
